refnamediv.refpurpose: Generates a storable representation of a value

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
stringserialize mixedvalue
Generates a storable representation of a value.
This is useful for storing or passing PHP values around without losing their type and structure.
To make the serialized string into a PHP value again, use unserialize.

&reftitle.parameters;
value
The value to be serialized. serialize handles all types, except that a resource is written as i:0;, without any diagnostic, and that some objects cannot be serialized (see note below). You can even serialize arrays that contain references to itself. A reference shared between several elements of the value, including a circular reference, is stored, and is restored by unserialize. A reference that occurs only once, or that is shared with a variable outside the value, is lost.
When serializing objects, PHP will attempt to call the member functions __serialize() or __sleep() prior to serialization. This is to allow the object to do any last minute clean-up, etc. prior to being serialized. Likewise, when the object is restored using unserialize the __unserialize() or __wakeup() member function is called. If the class defines __serialize(), it is used and __sleep() is ignored. Otherwise, if the class implements Serializable, its Serializable::serialize method is used (the C: format) before __sleep(). An enum case is written in the E: format. Uninitialized typed properties and static properties are not written; readonly properties are.
Object's private members have the class name prepended to the member name; protected members have a '*' prepended to the member name. These prepended values have null bytes on either side.

&reftitle.changelog;
&Version; &Description;
8.1.0
Enum cases are serialized in the E: format.
8.0.0
A name returned by __sleep() that is not a property is now skipped with an E_WARNING; previously it was serialized as &null; with an E_NOTICE.
7.4.0
__serialize() is now called.

&reftitle.notes;
Note that many built-in PHP objects cannot be serialized. However, those with this ability either implement the Serializable interface or the magic __serialize()/__unserialize() or __sleep()/__wakeup() methods. If an internal class does not fulfill any of those requirements, it cannot reliably be serialized.
There are some historical exceptions to the above rule, where some internal objects could be serialized without implementing the interface or exposing the methods.
When serialize serializes objects, the leading backslash is not included in the class name of namespaced classes for maximum compatibility.
